rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Pair creation:** a photon of at least 1.02 MeV (2 × 0.51 MeV, the two rest masses) converts to an electron–positron pair — but only near a nucleus, whose recoil conserves momentum. **Annihilation:** an electron and positron at rest destroy each other into two 0.51 MeV photons flying apart — two photons are mandatory for momentum conservation.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - γ → e⁻ + e⁺: E_min = 2m_ec² = 1.02 MeV - e⁻ + e⁺ → 2γ: each 0.51 MeV - Excess photon energy → kinetic energy

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Threshold Energy: Pair production requires photon energy ≥ 1.022 MeV (2 × electron rest energy). Below threshold, no pair creation.  ·  Third Body Required: Pair production cannot occur in vacuum — needs nucleus/electron to conserve momentum.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "A photon of energy at least 1.02 MeV can create an electron–positron pair in the field of a nucleus."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***PET scans*** — positrons annihilate in tissue; two 0.51 MeV photons are detected back-to-back.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Pair threshold = 1.02 MeV** (two rest masses); each annihilation photon = 0.51 MeV.  ·  **Two photons, not one, from annihilation** — momentum conservation demands it.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Matter Made and Unmade from Light A γ-ray photon with 1.02 MeV can turn into an electron and a positron; an electron meeting a positron vanishes into two photons. **Pair creation** and **annihilation** are E = mc² running in both directions — mass manufactured from energy and energy reclaimed from mass.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Pair creation A photon with energy ≥ 2m_ec² = **1.02 MeV**, passing close to a nucleus (needed for momentum conservation), can materialise into an **electron–positron pair**: $$\gamma \rightarrow e^- + e^+$$ - Threshold: 1.02 MeV — anything above goes into kinetic energy. - Charge is conserved: 0 → (−e) + (+e).…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (2m): A 1.53 MeV photon creates a pair. Find the pair's total KE.** — 1.53 − 1.02 = 0.51 MeV.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Write both equations with charges balanced.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **E = mc² in both directions** — light into matter, matter into light.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: γ → e⁻ + e⁺ (needs ≥ 1.02 MeV, near a nucleus); e⁻ + e⁺ → 2γ (0.51 MeV each).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Pair creation dominates γ-ray absorption above a few MeV; the photoelectric effect rules at low energies.

rows.text: ### Deep dive: energy ↔ matter, both directions with the books balanced Pair creation turns a photon into a particle–antiparticle pair; annihilation turns the pair back into photons.
